headline: Hearts of Pine presented a proposal to rezone part of 92 Cassidy Point Drive for a stadium, drawing public comment on the working waterfront.
summary: About 13 acres would move from the Waterfront Port Development Zone to B5 Urban Commercial, and about 9.2 acres on the south and west edges would stay in the port zone. A text change would also allow stadiums in B5, and the board is to make a recommendation to the City Council after a public hearing. Separately, the board approved a site plan for nine units at 101 and 105 Winter Street, along with three waivers.
decisions: Approved driveway spacing waiver of 23.43 feet and 36.92 feet, 7-0.
Approved five-inch curb reveal waiver on a roll call vote, all yes.
Approved waiver to allow two driveways on a roll call vote.
Approved site plan with conditions on a roll call vote.
Approved the approval letter as the board's decision on a roll call vote.
discussion: Cassidy Point economics: The applicant's study said the upland site lacks a viable industrial plan under current conditions. The city's waterfront coordinator presented data on the port's cargo, cruise, and seafood activity.
Working waterfront concerns: Several public speakers said the site should stay in working waterfront use. Others supported the stadium and the public access it would bring.

Contract zone options: Staff said a contract zone would be hard to use because stadiums are not allowed in the port zone. Members discussed narrowing the uses allowed in B5 or using an open space zone instead.
Winter Street project: A neighbor supported the project and said the two lots have been empty for a long time. The applicant said the historic preservation board was very supportive.
Hearing timing: The applicant said it is ready for a hearing as soon as possible. A December hearing was mentioned.
